parole.significato: roofing slate
parole.testo: From Ligurian abaìn, abæn. Compare abate (“abbot”) (slate dormers had the same grey color of an abbot's habit).

parole.significato: dormer (room)
parole.testo: From Ligurian abaìn, abæn. Compare abate (“abbot”) (slate dormers had the same grey color of an abbot's habit).

parole.significato: anchovy (any of the fish in the family Engraulidae family), particularly European anchovy (Engraulis encrasicolus)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ligurian anciôa, from Vulgar Latin *apiuva, from Latin aphyē, from Ancient Greek ἀφύη (aphúē).

parole.significato: to tighten (e.g. a rope)
parole.testo: Either Borrowed from Ligurian assuccâ (“to catch”) or from a- + Ligurian sùcca (“pumpkin”) + -are.

parole.significato: rope ladder
parole.testo: Probably from Ligurian.

parole.significato: hill, crag, ridgeside
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ligurian bric, from Proto-Celtic *brixs (“hill”). Doublet of borgo.

parole.significato: a mixture of foods used as bait
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ligurian, derived from Ancient Greek βρῶμα (brôma, “food; bait”).

parole.significato: an alley, especially one in Genoa
parole.testo: From Ligurian caróggio, from Vulgar Latin *quadruvium, for Classical Latin quadrivium (“crossroads”), from quattuor (“four”) + via (“road”). Doublet of carrobbio and of learned borrowing quadrivio. Compare Corsican carrughju and Sicilian carruggiu.

parole.significato: a scudo minted in the Republic of Genoa
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ligurian.

parole.significato: a dock (for ship to shore or repairs)
parole.testo: From Ligurian, from Arabic دَار الصِّنَاعَة (dār aṣ-ṣināʕa, “industry house, manufacturing shop”), from دَار (dār) + صِنَاعَة (ṣināʕa). Compare arsenale and arzanà. Cognate with Spanish dársena.

parole.significato: either of two varieties of focaccia, either from Genoa or from Venice
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ligurian fogassa and Venetan fogassa, from Late Latin focācia, plural of focācium. Doublet of focaccia.

parole.significato: synonym of gabbia (“crow's nest”)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ligurian gàggia, from Latin cavea, whence also gabbia and cavea.

parole.significato: A ceremonial cap worn by the doges of Genoa.
parole.testo: Ligurian gazzo, of unknown origin.

parole.significato: gutter rabbit (cat meat served as a substitute for rabbit)
parole.testo: Calque of Ligurian lêvre de cóppi (“gutter rabbit”).

parole.significato: jetty, pier, mole, quay, dock
parole.testo: Of Ligurian origin, from Ancient Greek μῶλος (môlos), μόλος (mólos), itself from Latin mōlēs.

parole.significato: to tinker with, to tamper
parole.testo: Related to Ligurian paciugo (“mud, slime”).

parole.significato: a sticky mixture, mud, slime
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ligurian [Term?].

parole.significato: a form of risotto from Piedmont and Lombardy
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ligurian panissa.

parole.significato: to eat (the bait) without taking the hook (of a fish)
parole.testo: From Ligurian [Term?] (“to peck”).

parole.significato: sheephead bream (Diplodus puntazzo)
parole.testo: From Ligurian.
